subject: physiology
title: Growth, puberty and ageing physiology

steps.tx: **Growth hormone** pulses from the pituitary, mediates through liver insulin like growth factor one, delays bone when thyroid fails, shows deficiency as short slow growth needing stimulation tests, and excess as gigantism before fusion or acromegaly after. Bone age by Greulich wrist films, percentile and velocity charts, mid parental target height, constitutional delay with bone matching delay, and familial short stature with bone matching age plot every child, and the puberty spurt accelerates the curve. Percentiles therefore track tempo as much as size.
steps.say: Pulsatile growth hormone works mostly through liver made insulin like growth factor one, the axis drawn in the figure, which is also the stable blood test for too much or too little. Plot height velocity against parental target: constitutional delay shows a late but normal pattern with delayed bone age, familial short stature shows short parents with normal bone age. Thyroid failure delays bone, deficiency needs stimulation testing, and excess enlarges hands and jaw after fusion.

vis.alt: Growth hormone axis: GHRH raises and somatostatin lowers growth hormone from the anterior pituitary; growth hormone stimulates IGF-1 from the liver, which acts on bone and tissues and feeds back to suppress growth hormone.
vis.caption: GH acts mostly through IGF-1; IGF-1 is the stable screening test for excess or deficiency.

steps.tx: **Puberty** wakes when gonadotropin releasing hormone pulses resume: thelarche buds breasts from eight to thirteen, pubarche hairs, menarche bleeds at twelve to thirteen, testicular volume reaches four millilitres first in boys, precocity before eight uses central analogues when central, and delay past fourteen without signs suggests Turner or Klinefelter syndromes. The adolescent spurt grows, androgens acne, limbic mood swings and prefrontal risk taking stage together, graded one to five by Tanner. Pulses therefore waken the gonadal axis in sleep first.
steps.say: Puberty begins when pulsatile gonadotropin releasing hormone wakes the pituitary gonadal axis in the diagram, breasts budding first in girls and testicular enlargement past four millilitres first in boys. Breast development before eight or no signs by fourteen by sex needs evaluation, central precocity answers to analogues, and Tanner stages one to five grade progress. Growth spurts, acne, mood change and risk taking travel together through adolescence.

vis.alt: Hypothalamic pituitary gonadal axis at puberty: pulsatile GnRH from the hypothalamus drives LH and FSH, which act on the gonads to make sex steroids and gametes, which cause secondary sexual characteristics; feedback is negative before puberty and set to allow cyclic surges in females.
vis.caption: Puberty starts when GnRH pulses wake up; the first sign is breast budding in girls and testicular enlargement in boys.

steps.tx: Untreated **hypothyroidism** in infancy dulls growth irreversibly as cretinism, caught by neonatal heel screening and replaced with thyroxine, while steroid excess stunts with Cushing moon weight and chronic coeliac, renal or asthma disease restores growth only when controlled. Nutrition fuels the curve with protein, zinc and vitamin D, and obesity advances bone age early. Heel screening therefore catches the silent thyroid before brains and bones pay, and dietitians plot weights and heights with families routinely until tempo recovers.
steps.say: A baby without thyroid hormone loses brain and bone growth permanently, which is why heel prick screening and prompt thyroxine are non negotiable. Excess steroids, coeliac disease, kidney disease or poorly controlled asthma each flatten velocity until the cause is treated. Protein, zinc and vitamin D fuel normal tempo, obesity advances bone age, and regular plotted measurements with the family catch faltering early.

steps.tx: **Ageing** brings menopause near fifty one with high follicle stimulating hormone and hormone choices for bones, gradual andropause testosterone fall, sarcopenia needing resistance exercise and protein, osteoporosis by DEXA needing bisphosphonates, vascular cognition needing training, and polypharmacy needing deprescribing. Geriatric assessment adds falls and vision, delirium by confusion assessment, frailty by grip strength, and vaccines against influenza, pneumococcus and zoster shielding. Years therefore tailor doses while pharmacists reconcile and stop anticholinergics routinely at every review.
steps.say: After fifty, ovaries fail, muscle mass and bone density fall, and medicines accumulate, the ageing row of the summary table. Resistance exercise with protein fights sarcopenia, bisphosphonates protect fragile bone, vascular risk training protects cognition, and vaccines shield against influenza, pneumococcus and shingles. Grip strength measures frailty, confusion screening catches delirium, and regular deprescribing removes anticholinergic burden.
